title: A running read-only reviewer blocks approval acceptance in every session of the same project, not just its own tree
outcome: While a read-only delegation runs, accepting an approval is refused only for sessions whose write scope actually overlaps the delegation's reviewed tree (and always in the read-only child itself), not for every session that shares the project.
acceptance: A behavioural test shows that while a read-only delegation reviews one worktree of a project, accepting an approval in a sibling session of the same project whose workdir neither contains nor lies inside the reviewed tree, or is separated from it by a Git worktree boundary, succeeds.

Behavioural tests show approval acceptance is still refused in the read-only child itself and in a session whose workdir overlaps the reviewed tree (inside it, or containing it without an intervening Git worktree boundary), with the existing message.

Other write actions routed through ensure_read_only_delegation_allows_write_action keep their existing tested protection unless a criterion-approved change says otherwise; the existing delegation_read_only tests stay green.

completion.summary: Approval acceptance is scoped to the reviewed tree while child identity and general project write protections remain.
